content: When I was first learning Lean, I benefitted tremendously from weekly meetings with @Heather Macbeth, who taught me the ropes in ways that I never could've picked up on my own. There are now a number of senior mathematicians who have expressed interest and eagerness to learn Lean properly (not just with AI, not that I have anything against that), but aren't as lucky as I was in finding Heather. Could this be something that the Mathlib Initiative helps to orchestrate? What I have in mind is a matchmaking service where younger folks who want to develop some part of the library could be paired with a senior expert in the field who wants to learn Lean. For example, does someone actively working on various aspects of Riemannian manifolds want to be paired with a distinguished senior researcher in the field? (If so, please DM me.)
ICARM's mission is to support and interact with the mathematics community, and we would be happy to help with the matchmaking if we can.
The purpose of the reviewer bootcamp that happened in Stockholm a few weeks ago is partly to set such a matchmaking up for reviewing

@Yaël Dillies can we get some kind of report on the reviewer bootcamp, e.g. a blog post? Nobody at the last mathlib community meeting had been so we've had no reports either formal or informal about what happened, what went well, lessons learnt etc.
